fields.oneLiner: PaathFee collects a tuition class's monthly fees over UPI and tells the teacher on the 5th which eleven students have not paid yet.
fields.jobStory:
When the first week of the month comes around at a neighbourhood tuition class with 90 students across six batches, the teacher wants the fee collection to have happened without her standing at the door asking children for envelopes, so I can spend that week teaching instead of doing accounts in a notebook at 10pm.

Who has this job: single-teacher tuition classes in Bhopal running out of a ground floor room or a rented hall, 60 to 150 students, fees between 500 and 1,500 rupees a month, classes 6 to 10 mostly maths and science. They are on the boards outside their own gate, they advertise in the local Hindi paper's classifieds, and about 240 of them are in one WhatsApp community for tuition-class owners that I was added to after an interview.

What they do instead: cash in an envelope with the student's name on it, entered into a register at night, and a phone call to the parent if the envelope does not arrive. Four of the seven teachers I sat with had started accepting UPI to their personal number, which made it worse rather than better, because now the payment and the name are in two different places and matching a 900 rupee credit to a child takes longer than opening an envelope.
fields.trafficTestNotes:
One source only, and I want to be upfront about that. On 6 September a teacher I interviewed added me to a WhatsApp community for tuition-class owners in Bhopal, 240 members. I asked the admin and posted once on 7 Sep: a short message about the envelope-and-register problem, a photo of a register page with a column of missing ticks, and the link. I posted once and did not re-post.

Numbers: the short link shows 34 clicks. 19 of those signed up, which is 56%. Spend was zero rupees. I did not run ads this round because I wanted to see whether the pitch lands before paying to put it anywhere.

On the 56%: it is a small sample and a warm room. These are 240 people who all have exactly this job, reading a message about their own problem from somebody whose name the admin vouched for. I would not expect anything close to that from a cold ad. What I take from it is that the description of the problem is right, not that the demand number is right. Next round is a paid Meta test to a cold audience in Bhopal and Indore so I have a number I can compare against.

notes: Borderline, and a careful human could go either way. One free channel, 34 visits and a 56% conversion is a thin test, and a stricter reviewer would return it on traffic-test for the single warm community and zero spend. We pass it because the bar asks for a named source with reach, visits, signups and spend and all four are reported, the community is not the student's own cohort or family, and clause 9 is answered head on - he explains the 56% and says what it does and does not prove.
